# `silk/cli/progress`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Progress of long work on standard error: a live line redrawn in place on a terminal, and one
plain line for each finished step elsewhere.

## When to use
Use [`Progress`](#Progress) in a command line program for work that takes more than a moment, such as a
download, a signature check, or unpacking an archive, so that the program never looks stuck.
`NativeHttp.reportProgress` from `silk.http.client_native` feeds a download into one.

## Details
Pick a [`ProgressStyle`](#ProgressStyle) once, usually with [`ProgressStyle.standardError`](#ProgressStyle.impl.standardError), and make one
[`Progress`](#Progress) with it. Each step opens with [`Progress.begin`](#Progress.impl.begin), counts its work with
[`Progress.advance`](#Progress.impl.advance), and closes with [`Progress.finish`](#Progress.impl.finish) or [`Progress.abandon`](#Progress.impl.abandon).

- `Live`: one line, redrawn in place at most every 80 ms: a spinner, the label, a bar when the
  total is known, the amount done, and for bytes the rate and the time left. A finished step
  leaves a row with a check mark, its summary, its size and its time.
- `Plain`: no escape codes. Only the row of a finished step is written.
- `Off`: nothing is written and no clock is read.

Output never fails the work: a failed write to standard error is dropped.

## Gotchas
The live line assumes that nothing else writes to standard error while a step is open. Finish
or abandon the step before you print.

## Examples
### Count the bytes of a step
```silk
import silk.cli.progress { Progress, ProgressStyle, ProgressUnit }
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }

effect fn copy(progress: &mut Progress) -> () ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator {
  run progress.begin("Downloading data.bin", ProgressUnit.Bytes, 4096)
  run progress.advance(1024)
  run progress.advance(3072)
  run progress.finish("Downloaded data.bin")
}

pub effect fn main() -> i32 ! OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  // An `Off` style writes nothing, as standard error of a test should stay quiet.
  let mut progress = Progress.make(ProgressStyle.off())
  run copy(&mut progress) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  if progress.done() != 4096 || progress.isOpen() {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `Progress` with `import silk.cli.progress { Progress }`.

## `ProgressStyle`

```silk
pub struct ProgressStyle
```

How progress is shown: the display, whether rows use color, and the terminal width the live
line must fit in.

### Details
[`ProgressStyle.standardError`](#ProgressStyle.impl.standardError) picks a style for standard error. [`ProgressStyle.off`](#ProgressStyle.impl.off) writes
nothing.

<a id="ProgressStyle.impl.standardError"></a>

### Associated function `standardError`

```silk
pub effect fn standardError() -> ProgressStyle
    ! HostInputError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut HostInput | &mut Allocator
```

The style for standard error: `Live` on a terminal, `Plain` otherwise.

#### Details
A terminal whose `TERM` is `dumb` gets `Plain`. Only `Live` uses color, unless `NO_COLOR` is
set and not empty.
The width is the terminal's own where the target can ask for it, else `COLUMNS`, else 80.

#### Errors
- `HostInputError` or `OutOfMemoryError` if the environment cannot be read.

<a id="Progress"></a>

## `Progress`

```silk
pub struct Progress
```

The progress of one step at a time, written to standard error in a [`ProgressStyle`](#ProgressStyle).

### Details
A step opens with [`Progress.begin`](#Progress.impl.begin) and closes with [`Progress.finish`](#Progress.impl.finish), which leaves a row,
or [`Progress.abandon`](#Progress.impl.abandon), which leaves nothing. Counting a closed step does nothing, so code that
feeds a `Progress`, such as a download, can run with or without an open step.

<a id="Progress.impl.begin"></a>

### Method `begin`

```silk
pub effect fn begin(self: &mut Self, label: string, unit: ProgressUnit, total: u64) -> ()
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Opens a step named `label`, such as `Downloading silk.tar.gz`, that counts `unit` up to
`total`, or zero when the total is not known yet.

#### Details
A step that is still open is abandoned first. The live line is drawn at once.

#### Errors
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` fails.
